action.instructions: Follow the ordered reference route closely while making forward progress through the CURRENT checkpoint. Coordinates are [forward metres, left metres] relative to the boat at sampling: [+,0] ahead, [0,+] LEFT, [0,-] RIGHT. The ordered ahead route points describe the upcoming dashed route, not separate checkpoints. Stay near that curve throughout the movement; do not shortcut bends just to reach a distant checkpoint. Enter the current checkpoint circle before proceeding to later route points. Choose ONE speed/course pair. Each option specifies a TARGET heading offset relative to the CURRENT sampled bow, once. It is not an angular acceleration or turn-rate command. Positive offsets mean LEFT, negative RIGHT. Speed and heading follow the response rules below. Each option states the resulting end position in CURRENT boat coordinates. Positive speed moves along the INSTANTANEOUS bow, negative opposite it, while the bow may still be turning. Prefer positive speed when equivalent movement is available. Compare the movement segment with the nearby route and current checkpoint. Use a smaller nonzero speed near sharp bends or when a full step would overshoot. Do not choose stop merely because you are on the route or inside an intermediate checkpoint; continue making progress. Judge LEFT versus RIGHT using the signs in the CURRENT coordinate frame, even after the last action changed the boat heading. For example, nearby route points [1,0],[2,0] call for ahead motion; account for residual yaw before selecting another turn. [1,1],[2,2] indicate ahead-LEFT, while [1,-1],[2,-2] indicate ahead-RIGHT. Follow the NEAREST supplied ahead route points first; the far checkpoint does not justify departing from that portion. If already close to the route, do not create a large sideways deviation. When the curve is between the available directions, alternate short movements rather than long zigzags. Prefer smaller displacement when it reduces departure from the curve. At the final target, target zero speed if already inside the arrival circle; there is no need to reach its exact centre. If target.forward_left_m[0] is negative, that checkpoint is BEHIND the sampled bow. Slow down and turn back toward it; never keep charging ahead away from an unpassed checkpoint. A large cross_track_distance_m calls for recovery toward the near route, not maximum-speed forward travel. A CHANGED target speed starts CONSTANT ACCELERATION immediately: a=(target_speed-current_speed)/speed_transition_time_s. It reaches the target exactly after speed_transition_time_s of SIMULATION time, then holds it. There is NO waiting delay before acceleration and no exponential response or damping. Keeping active_target_speed_mps continues the existing ramp for remaining_transition_s; it does NOT restart the transition clock. A different target starts a new full-duration ramp. Current signed speed is boat.speed_mps. A stop option targets zero but DOES NOT instantly stop motion. Each option gives the integrated end position and end speed, accounting for this lag. When reversing signed speed, motion may first continue in the old signed direction. Use smaller target speeds before bends and the final circle. To park, reduce speed before arrival and target zero early enough to remain inside the circle while slowing. While inside the final circle with residual speed, continue targeting zero; do not add thrust just because completion needs another interval. Heading changes GRADUALLY with CONTINUOUS yaw rate. A changed target uses the shortest signed heading difference and a cubic curve starting at the CURRENT yaw rate and ending at the target heading with ZERO yaw after heading_response.transition_time_s. This is an immediate angular-acceleration process, not a waiting delay or instant rotation. The current yaw can carry the bow briefly the old way before reversing. Keeping the same WORLD target heading continues its remaining_transition_s. Relative option offsets refer to the sampled bow, not the previous target, so repeatedly choosing a nonzero offset can keep moving the target. Motion during turning is CURVED: use each option midpoint, endpoint and final yaw. AHEAD targets the sampled heading; with residual yaw it brakes and returns toward that heading. The CURRENT target is an intermediate CHECKPOINT: entering its circle is sufficient; no stop is required.
